tau_road_south.title: The Road South
tau_road_south.description: Wrangler Tull drove kodo down the Great Lift twice a year for most of his life. The Lift is gone. So is the cliff it hung on, and in their place is a mountain that has stood there four years and has never been explained to anybody's satisfaction. Taurajo has had no word from anything south of it since - not Freewind, not the flats, not the salt crews.
tau_road_south.accept_text: I am not asking you to fix it. I am asking you to walk up and look at it, because I have asked four people and got four different mountains back. Go to where the Lift stood. The winch house is still bolted to the rock and the cable runs out thirty feet and straight into granite. Past that there is a line in the ground where red dust stops and leaf mould starts, sharp as a knife cut. Stand on it. Tell me what is on the other side.
tau_road_south.turn_in_text: Trees. You are standing there telling me there are trees. I drove that road twenty years. There was sky and a very long drop and nothing else on it, and now there are trees growing out of the part where the drop used to be. Sit down. I need a moment with that.

org_new_border.title: What We Border Now
org_new_border.description: Elder Torgun's work is knowing where the Horde's edges are and what stands on the other side of them. For four years the southern edge of the Barrens has been a mountain range nobody charted, and the best report Orgrimmar holds was written by a scout who walked to the treeline and came back down the same afternoon. The Warchief does not need the mountain described. He needs to know whether anything is coming off it.
org_new_border.accept_text: Go up to the escarpment - the long drop where the Lift's cliff used to be. Garuk Emberhide has been on it a season and will give you the short version, which is the only version he has. The harpies are what I care about. Barrens harpies, roosting on a mountain, nesting on bare rock instead of the crags they hatched in. Thin them where you find them and count what you see.
org_new_border.turn_in_text: Pushed up. Not moved in. That is a different report and a considerably worse one. If that range took their ground when it landed, then it took somebody else's as well, and whoever that was has gone somewhere. Nobody has asked where. I am going to start asking.

hbe_impossible_yetis.title: A Matter of Impossibility
hbe_impossible_yetis.description: Apothecary Lydon has given eleven years to Alterac yeti and is the authority on them, largely because nobody competed for the position. A caravan master came through Tarren Mill with a story about yeti on the far side of the world, in a desert province of Kalimdor, and Lydon has not been able to put it down. Yeti do not cross oceans. Yeti do not cross rivers. The caravan master was extremely sure.
hbe_impossible_yetis.accept_text: I am not asking you to believe it. I am asking you to carry this across an ocean, put it in the hand of whoever is senior at that logging camp, and let them tell me I have wasted my time and theirs. It is sealed. Do not open it. The questions inside are embarrassing and I would like them answered before they are laughed at.
hbe_impossible_yetis.turn_in_text: He writes a very careful letter for a man who has already made up his mind. Tell him yes. Tell him there are yeti in this mountain, that they did not walk here, and that all of us would sleep better if his impossibility had held.

asp_winch_house.title: What the Winch House Kept
asp_winch_house.description: Keeper Nalu worked the north winch eleven years and was off shift the morning the ground changed. The house is still standing because the house was always on the Barrens side. The ledgers are still in it. So is a season of mail that was stacked and waiting to go down and never went. She has come back up most weeks for four years and has not once been able to open the box.
asp_winch_house.accept_text: The ledgers are in the iron chest under the drum. Three of them, if the damp has left me three. The mail is loose in the sorting rack and some of it will have blown into the scrub by now - bring whatever is still readable. I know roughly what is in most of it. I would still rather hold it than keep guessing.
asp_winch_house.turn_in_text: This one is a girl in Freewind writing to her brother on the top side. Dated the week before. She is telling him about a horse. I am not going to be able to deliver it and I am going to keep it anyway, and I would thank you not to have an opinion about that.

asp_cable_run.title: Thirty Feet and Into Rock
asp_cable_run.description: The main cable still comes off the drum and runs the thirty feet it always ran, and then it goes into the granite as though the granite had grown around it. Which, Nalu will point out in a very level voice, is approximately what happened. The rock did not fall on the cable. The rock arrived where the cable already was.
asp_cable_run.accept_text: Follow it down to the face and look at where it enters. The harpies have been at the loose ends - they want the wire for their nests and they have taken what they could reach. Bring me four pieces and I can tell you how it parted. Mind the rim. It is a long way down and there are only a few places to do it on purpose.
asp_cable_run.turn_in_text: Two of these are cut clean. The others are sheared, and wire only shears like that under load. So the cable was carrying when the ground came. Something was on it. I have spent four years not thinking that, and I would like you to know you have ended a fairly useful habit.

asp_wrong_side.title: The Wrong Side of the Line
asp_wrong_side.description: Watcher Tomak keeps the Seam, which in practice means watching things die slowly on the wrong side of it. The kodo are the worst. Barrens animals standing in snow, four years into a winter their kind has no word for, at a line they will not cross back over because there is nothing on the other side of it any more either.
asp_wrong_side.accept_text: I will not dress it up for you. They are suffering, they are going to keep suffering, and the only thing anyone can do for them is the thing nobody volunteers for. Ten of them. Do it clean and do it from the front, because they will not run and it is worse if you make them try to.
asp_wrong_side.turn_in_text: My grandmother drove kodo. I grew up with one breathing against the tent flap all night. You did it properly, and from the front, and that is not nothing. Most people do it from behind so they do not have to see the face.

asp_red_ground.title: A Handful of Home
asp_red_ground.description: The camp downslope has lived under trees for four years and has not once stood on its own ground. Tomak has been quietly carrying Barrens soil down off the Seam, a sack at a time. It will not grow anything. It is for the floor of the elder's lodge, so that there is red dirt under somebody's feet when something important is being said over it.
asp_red_ground.accept_text: Take it off the dust side of the line, not the mould side. It has to be the real thing or there is no point in carrying it anywhere. The scavengers will be on you the whole time - they nest in the dead scrub and they have worked out that a person crouching is a person not watching. Deal with them first, if you have sense.
asp_red_ground.turn_in_text: It goes under the lodge floor tonight. Mura will stand on it and say nothing about it, and every single person in that camp will know what they are standing on, and that is how it should be done.

asp_rope_trade.title: An Honest Opportunity
asp_rope_trade.description: Fizzik Quickline arrived on the rim with forty coils of rope and the unshakeable conviction that a cliff with no road down it is the finest business proposition on the continent. He is correct. He is also nearly out of rope, and the only thing up here strong enough to replace it is harpy sinew, a sentence he delivers far too cheerfully.
asp_rope_trade.accept_text: Windcallers first. The plain ones mob you, but it is the callers that turn a mob into a problem, and I would prefer you came back, because you are a repeat customer and those are precious. Ten coils sees me through the season. I pay fair, which in my family is treated as a confession.
asp_rope_trade.turn_in_text: Fair is fair. And listen - the ways down are free. I am not charging anybody for knowing where a gully is. Rope is a product. Knowing things is advertising. There is a difference and my cousins have never understood it.

asp_ways_down.title: Four Ways Down
asp_ways_down.description: Ash Winterfall runs the chutes, which every elder in the camp has told him not to do. A chute is an avalanche path - swept bare every few winters by something enormous coming down it - and that scouring is exactly what makes it the only walkable line on a face of loose rock. The dangerous ground and the only road are the same ground. He finds this funnier than they do.
asp_ways_down.accept_text: Three of the four. Take the middle one first, under the Lift - it is the widest, and if you cannot manage that one you have no business on the others. Then the west gully and the east. Walk them, do not run them, and do not do it late on a warm afternoon when the sun has been sitting on the snowfield all day. That is when they go.
asp_ways_down.turn_in_text: That is the zone, then. Everything below the rim can be reached and everything above it is just the Barrens with a better view. Two winters I have been asking the elders for a proper trail crew. Perhaps they will listen to somebody who has actually been down the thing.

asp_rim_harpies.title: Nesting Where They Should Not
asp_rim_harpies.description: Garuk has been counting harpies since the thaw and does not care for the number. On the escarpment he can at least make sense of them - it is rock, it is a cliff, it is the kind of place a harpy belongs. It is the ones further down that trouble him. Harpies roosting in aspen crowns. In trees. Harpies do not do that, and something has taught them to.
asp_rim_harpies.accept_text: Work the rim first, then the stands beneath it. The tree-roosters are the dangerous ones. You do not see them until they are already dropping, and they have learned to wait, which is a word I do not enjoy using about harpies. I am not asking for a cull. I am asking for enough of a dent that I can tell Orgrimmar the number went down once.
asp_rim_harpies.turn_in_text: Good. Write the tally in your own hand and I will send it under mine. Two witnesses is the difference between a report and a rumour, and the Warchief has had four years of rumours about this mountain. He has had quite enough of them from people who came off that other world, as well, which I am not saying to be unkind. I am saying it because you will be asked.

asp_the_load.title: What Was On The Cable
asp_the_load.description: You turn the wire over in your hands. Lift cable, the heavy grade, wound into the base of a harpy nest with the patience of something that simply liked the shape of it. The end has not been cut. It has been drawn out thin and snapped - the way wire goes when it is pulled past what it can hold. Something was hanging on this when the ground changed.
asp_the_load.accept_text: Nalu Stillgrass kept that winch eleven years. She will know what a loaded cable end looks like and she will know what an empty one looks like, and she will not thank you for the difference. Take it to her. Look at the face under the Lift on the way, where the main line enters the rock, and see whether there is anything below it.
asp_the_load.turn_in_text: She does not say anything for a long moment. Then: "Full car. Going down." She puts the wire in the iron chest with the ledgers, closes the lid, and sets her hand flat on top of it, and that is the end of the conversation for today.

asp_green_wood.title: Green Wood, Dry Wood
asp_green_wood.description: Hateg Barkhand has been told aspen is poor timber by three separate people who had never put a hand on it. Green, it is heavy and soaking and splits like wet rope. Seasoned, it goes light as nothing and takes a nail without argument. The camp has been seasoning it wrong for two winters because everything any of them knew about wood was about a different wood, on a different continent, under a different sky.
asp_green_wood.accept_text: Standing dead, not fallen. Fallen has been lying in the wet and it is no use to me whatever it looks like on the outside. Twelve bolts will tell me whether the rot runs up from the root or down from the crown. Watch the lynx while you are cutting - they lie up in the deadfall and you will be bent over with an axe and your back to the slope.
asp_green_wood.turn_in_text: Down from the crown. Every single one. So we have been stacking it upside down for two winters, in the rain, on purpose. Two winters. Do not tell Mura. I want to tell Mura.

asp_first_planks.title: The First Good Planks
asp_first_planks.description: Knowing which way the rot runs is not the same as having a floor. Longstand has a saw, a pile of bolts stacked the right way up at last, and not one person who has cut a board that came out true. Hateg would like the first honest stack this camp has produced, and he would like somebody else's hands on the saw while he stands behind them and watches what they do wrong.
asp_first_planks.accept_text: Six boards. Not six attempts - six I would put in a wall. The whole thing is the first cut. Get that off true and every board after it is off true, and you will not find out until the wall is up and the door will not close. Take your time on the first one. The rest follow it whether you want them to or not.
asp_first_planks.turn_in_text: That is a stack of boards. That is an actual stack of actual boards. My father raised a tent frame every spring of his life and never once needed a plank for anything. I am going to think about that later, when I am less pleased with myself.

asp_winter_meat.title: Meat for a Winter We Do Not Know
asp_winter_meat.description: Sani Quietstep hunted open plain her whole life, where you find a herd at dawn and you have it by noon and the only question is how far you want to carry it. Up here the elk walk into timber and stop existing. She has got better at it. She is not good at it yet, and the camp has to eat through a winter nobody has measured.
asp_winter_meat.accept_text: Work the edges of the stands, not the middle. They cross between cover in the same places every day, and up here that is the only predictable thing about them. Eight good haunches. Leave the thin ones - we are not so short that we take a poor animal, and I would rather not find out what we become once we start.
asp_winter_meat.turn_in_text: Eight, and not a thin one among them. You hunted the edges. I will be good at this in another two winters. I would rather have stayed bad at it on open ground, but nobody asked me and nobody is going to.

asp_wolf_nights.title: The Nights Are Loud
asp_wolf_nights.description: Mura Longstand will tell you the wolves are not the problem, and she is right. They were here before the camp and they have taken nothing but offal. The problem is that nobody in the camp sleeps, because the pack works the dark timber behind the sheds, and every person in Longstand grew up somewhere you could see a thing coming from a long way off.
asp_wolf_nights.accept_text: Thin the pack on the north side where the lodgepole starts. Not all of them. I will not have it said that we came into somebody else's country and emptied it. The bears are a separate matter. One has been at the smokehouse and has stopped being frightened of people, and that is the point at which it stops being a bear and starts being a problem.
asp_wolf_nights.turn_in_text: The camp will sleep tonight. That is worth more than people who have always slept would guess at. And you left some. Good. A place with nothing in the dark is not a safer place. It is only an emptier one, and I have seen what empty looks like.

asp_uphill_boar.title: They Did Not Want To Come Either
asp_uphill_boar.description: Owen Tallgrass watches Elkhorn because it is the only place in this zone where you can see anything at all. What he has been watching is quilboar coming up out of the Barrens in numbers, into a cold they have no clothing for and no word for. They were pushed. The mountain took their ground the same week it took the Lift. He points this out to people and it has never once made anybody friendlier.
asp_uphill_boar.accept_text: The highrunners work the meadow edges at first light. They are fast and they are desperate, and those are two different problems arriving at the same time. Drop the frostspeakers first. Four years they have been trying to pray the cold back down, and whatever it is they are actually doing, it is the thing keeping the rest of them on their feet.
asp_uphill_boar.turn_in_text: That will hold them off the meadow until the thaw. Then they will come back, because they still have nowhere else to be, and we will do all of this again. I would like somebody cleverer than me to think about that part. I have been waiting four years for somebody to volunteer.

asp_broken_dams.title: The Benches Are Flooding
asp_broken_dams.description: Gelt Rivermane's benches are a stair of beaver ponds, and the dams have held every spring without anybody's help since long before the camp arrived. This year three have gone inside a month. The quilboar have been cutting them, and not for the timber - for the water. A drained pond is dry ground to den in, and a dencarver would flood a whole valley before he spent another winter wet.
asp_broken_dams.accept_text: The dencarvers are down at the third pond and they have got good at it, which is the part that bothers me. Bring the timber back up when you are done. The beavers will rebuild - they always rebuild - but they rebuild faster with their own sticks than with new ones, and I am long past caring whether that is sentimental.
asp_broken_dams.turn_in_text: They were back on it before you were out of the water. Did you see? Four years I have watched them put this valley together again every spring, with no plan and no elders and no argument about it. There is a lesson in that and I am too tired tonight to say what it is.

asp_surveyors_pin.title: Somebody Measured This
asp_surveyors_pin.description: You turn it over. A surveyor's pin, brass, stamped with a number and a maker's mark you have never seen - and it was in a quilboar den, wrapped in hide, kept. The number is the part that stops you. Numbered pins come in a sequence, and a sequence means somebody walked this ground with a chain and a book and wrote down what they found, before any of this was here.
asp_surveyors_pin.accept_text: Hesta Coldshoulder keeps the watch up near the ice and she has an eye for things that do not add up, which is most of this mountain. She will know whether that mark is Horde, Alliance, or neither. The dencarvers will have more of them. They have been turning over this whole valley and keeping anything that shines.
asp_surveyors_pin.turn_in_text: She holds it to the light a long while. "Not ours," she says. "Not theirs either." She hands it back. "You came off that other world. Does that mark mean anything to you?" And she watches your face very carefully while you answer, and says nothing at all about what she sees there.

asp_higher_every_spring.title: Higher Every Spring
asp_higher_every_spring.description: Hesta Coldshoulder has been measuring the creek on the benches for three years with a stick and a notch, which she is perfectly aware is not science. It is higher every spring. Not by much. By enough that she can no longer explain it with snowfall, and the water is coming out of a hole in the rim that was not a hole when she started counting.
asp_higher_every_spring.accept_text: The mouth is on the east side of the rim, above the old slide. You will feel it before you see it - the air coming out of that hole is wrong for this mountain. Go in as far as the shaft where the daylight comes down and no further this trip. I want to know what the floor is. If it is wet rock, then I am right about where my water is going.
asp_higher_every_spring.turn_in_text: Wet rock. Four years ago that was ice, and in four more it will be a room. The range did not arrive empty. It brought a glacier inside it, and the glacier is dying, and that is what has been running down into my ponds.

asp_the_thaw.title: What the Thaw Lets Go
asp_the_thaw.description: A glacier holds on to everything it ever picked up, and a melting one hands it all back in roughly the order it took it. Hesta wants whatever the ice has been letting go of this spring, before the meltwater carries it down the creek and into the ponds where she will never find it. She would also like considerably fewer bears in there.
asp_the_thaw.accept_text: Work the wet end, near the shaft. That is where the ice is going fastest and that is where things are coming out of the wall. The bears denned in that cave when it was only a cave and they are not pleased about the company they have acquired. They are nearest the door for the same reason you will be: it is the only warm part of the place. Mind that you are not between them and the way out.
asp_the_thaw.turn_in_text: A bone pin. A button. And something I am not going to guess at in front of you. None of it is tauren work and none of it is orcish. The ice picked these up somewhere else entirely and has just now put them down here. That is the second time this month I have had to write that sentence, and I did not care for it the first time.

asp_cornered_cold.title: Cornered in the Cold
asp_cornered_cold.description: The query from Tarren Mill asked whether there are yeti in Kalimdor. Mura Longstand's answer is that there are, that they are at the frozen end of a cave which is getting smaller every single year, and that she does not enjoy either half of that sentence. They came across inside the ice. Nobody carried them. They are refugees of the same accident that moved her people, and she has noticed, and it has not changed what has to be done.
asp_cornered_cold.accept_text: They are pressed into the deep end where the ice still holds, and they come out as far as the standing water to feed. Go in by the shaft and work inward. It gets colder and it gets older and they get worse the further you go. If you meet the big one before you are ready for him, come back out. He will still be there. He has nowhere else.
asp_cornered_cold.turn_in_text: You went further in than I asked. You generally do. I will write to the apothecary now. I will tell him his impossible thing is real, that it is cornered, and that it is running out of cave. He will be pleased. I have thought about it for a week and I cannot find the part I am supposed to be pleased about.

asp_rimehowl.title: The Last Cold Place
asp_rimehowl.description: At the far end of the Weeping Ice, past the braided passages and the standing meltwater, the glacier is still a glacier. The water drains down into it and does not come back out. That is where Rimehowl is, and he is there because it is the last ground left that is what he was made for. He will not leave it. There is nowhere to leave it to.
asp_rimehowl.accept_text: The Sink. Follow the water down and it will take you there - that is the one thing water does reliably in that cave. He is bigger than the others and he is not stupid. He will give ground and let the cold do his work for him, so do not let a long fight become his fight. And take people with you. I am not sending you in alone and I would not go in alone.
asp_rimehowl.turn_in_text: It is done, then. I am not going to stand here and tell you I am glad. He was the last of something, standing in the last of somewhere, and the only reason he was ever a danger to anybody is that his country melted out from under him. Ours went as well. We walked south. He could not.

asp_what_came_across.title: What Else Came Across
asp_what_came_across.description: Mura Longstand has set two facts beside one another and does not care for the shape they make. A mountain arrived. Inside it was a glacier, and inside the glacier were animals that have no business on this continent and did not walk here to get to it. The range did not come empty. It came with its own country folded up inside it, and in four years nobody has asked how much of that country is still alive in there.
asp_what_came_across.accept_text: I have put the hide, the hair and the apothecary's own letter into one bundle with my mark burned into the wrap. Take it down to Tull at Taurajo. Four years ago that man asked whether there was still a road south. The honest answer is that there is no road, there is a mountain, and the mountain has things living in it that are not from here and never were. He will want to be sitting down for the second part.
asp_what_came_across.turn_in_text: Tull reads it through twice, then lays his hand flat on the table on top of it. "So it is not a wall," he says. "It is a country. Somebody else's country, dropped on top of ours, and we have spent four years treating it like weather." He does not say anything else for a long time, and he does not move his hand.
